summary: Final check, then the run ends on its budget: I re-read startStopReplication in the captured source to confirm the load-bearing premise of the VerifyLeader finding, and it holds — the loop registers replication state for every server in the latest configuration with only a self-check, no suffrage filter, so nonvoters are registered for verify notifications and their acknowledgements can reach the tally while the quorum counts voters only. That premise had been read once early in the run and is relied on in the finding, so verifying it rather than assuming it was the last thing worth doing; it confirmed rather than changed anything, which is why no new record is added. The run's results stand as recorded: the RestoreCommittedLogs startup replay blocks NewRaft once the committed-but-unapplied window exceeds the FSM channel's batch capacity, with the boundary measured at 128 batches and the default snapshot settings in force; VerifyLeader accepts nonvoter acknowledgements toward a voter quorum, and under per-node timers that confirmation outlived a competing leader's election in twenty of twenty trials and coincided with committed state the confirming leader had never applied in twelve of twelve, while uniform clusters kept the separation down to a one-millisecond margin; and AddVoter installs a Voter immediately against two published descriptions that promise staging, which can strand a single-voter cluster until the added server runs. Five suspicions were refuted with evidence, one behaviour entry was corrected under its own id with its affected use answered, every registered question is answered, and no necessary gap remains.
